views.name: customer_payments_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  payment.payment_id,
  payment.customer_id AS customer_id,
  payment.amount AS payment_amount,
  payment.payment_date AS payment_date
FROM payment
views.description: All payment records with their customer reference, payment amount, and payment date (no aggregation), serving as the raw cohort of payments to analyze.

views.name: customer_monthly_totals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  strftime('%Y-%m', payment_date) AS year_month,
  SUM(payment_amount) AS month_total_amount
FROM customer_payments_raw
GROUP BY customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', payment_date)
views.description: For each customer and calendar month (derived from payment_date), sum all payments in that month to produce one total payment amount per customer-month.

views.name: customer_monthly_diffs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cmt.customer_id,
  cmt.year_month,
  cmt.month_total_amount,
  ABS(cmt.month_total_amount - COALESCE(
    LAG(cmt.month_total_amount) OVER (
      PARTITION BY cmt.customer_id
      ORDER BY cmt.year_month
    ), 0
  )) AS abs_monthly_diff
FROM customer_monthly_totals AS cmt
views.description: For each customer-month row, compute the absolute difference in month_total_amount between this month and the previous calendar month for that same customer (using ordering by year_month).

views.name: customer_avg_monthly_change
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cmd.customer_id,
  AVG(cmd.abs_monthly_diff) AS avg_monthly_change,
  COUNT(cmd.abs_monthly_diff) AS diff_count
FROM
  customer_monthly_diffs AS cmd
GROUP BY
  cmd.customer_id
HAVING
  COUNT(cmd.abs_monthly_diff) >= 1
views.description: For each customer, compute the average of abs_monthly_diff across their consecutive-month differences, and keep only customers who have at least one difference (i.e., at least two distinct months).

views.name: customer_purchases
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id AS customer_id,
  payment_date AS purchase_timestamp,
  amount AS purchase_amount
FROM payment
views.description: All purchase events with their customer identifier, purchase timestamp, and purchase amount. This is the base cohort of purchase rows (no aggregation), used to compute per-customer metrics and initial-purchase times.

views.name: customer_first_purchase
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  customer_id,
  MIN(payment_date) AS first_purchase_timestamp
FROM payment
GROUP BY customer_id
views.description: Each customer's initial purchase timestamp (earliest purchase). One row per customer with their first_purchase_timestamp.

views.name: customer_time_buckets_sales
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cp.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cp.purchase_timestamp AS purchase_timestamp,
  cp.purchase_amount AS purchase_amount,
  CASE
    WHEN cp.purchase_timestamp >= cfp.first_purchase_timestamp
     AND cp.purchase_timestamp < datetime(cfp.first_purchase_timestamp, '+7 days')
    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_in_first_7_days,
  CASE
    WHEN cp.purchase_timestamp >= cfp.first_purchase_timestamp
     AND cp.purchase_timestamp < datetime(cfp.first_purchase_timestamp, '+30 days')
    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_in_first_30_days,
  CASE
    WHEN cp.purchase_timestamp >= cfp.first_purchase_timestamp
     AND cp.purchase_timestamp < datetime(cfp.first_purchase_timestamp, '+7 days')
    THEN cp.purchase_amount ELSE 0 END AS amount_in_first_7_days,
  CASE
    WHEN cp.purchase_timestamp >= cfp.first_purchase_timestamp
     AND cp.purchase_timestamp < datetime(cfp.first_purchase_timestamp, '+30 days')
    THEN cp.purchase_amount ELSE 0 END AS amount_in_first_30_days
FROM customer_purchases cp
JOIN customer_first_purchase cfp
  ON cp.customer_id = cfp.customer_id
views.description: Join purchases to each customer's first purchase timestamp and compute, per purchase row, flags or bucketed amounts indicating whether the purchase falls into the first 7-day interval [first, first+7*24h) and into the first 30-day interval [first, first+30*24h). Keeps original purchase amount and these bucketed amounts per purchase.

views.name: customer_ltv_and_first_period_shares
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cp.customer_id AS customer_id,
  SUM(cp.payment_amount) AS ltv,
  SUM(CASE WHEN julianday(cp.payment_date) - julianday(cf.first_purchase_timestamp) <= 7 THEN cp.payment_amount ELSE 0 END) AS first_7_days_sales,
  SUM(CASE WHEN julianday(cp.payment_date) - julianday(cf.first_purchase_timestamp) <= 30 THEN cp.payment_amount ELSE 0 END) AS first_30_days_sales,
  CASE WHEN SUM(cp.payment_amount) > 0 THEN SUM(CASE WHEN julianday(cp.payment_date) - julianday(cf.first_purchase_timestamp) <= 7 THEN cp.payment_amount ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / SUM(cp.payment_amount) ELSE NULL END AS pct_first_7,
  CASE WHEN SUM(cp.payment_amount) > 0 THEN SUM(CASE WHEN julianday(cp.payment_date) - julianday(cf.first_purchase_timestamp) <= 30 THEN cp.payment_amount ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / SUM(cp.payment_amount) ELSE NULL END AS pct_first_30
FROM customer_payments_raw cp
JOIN customer_first_purchase cf USING (customer_id)
GROUP BY cp.customer_id
HAVING SUM(cp.payment_amount) > 0
views.description: Aggregate per customer to compute total lifetime sales (ltv), sum of amounts within first 7 days, and sum within first 30 days, then compute per-customer share: pct_first_7 = first7 / ltv and pct_first_30 = first30 / ltv. Exclude customers with ltv = 0 in this relation (so downstream averages only include customers with positive LTV).

views.name: film_revenues_valid
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.film_id AS film_id,
  f.title AS film_title,
  SUM(p.amount) AS film_total_revenue
FROM film f
JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
JOIN rental r ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
JOIN payment p ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
GROUP BY f.film_id, f.title
HAVING film_total_revenue IS NOT NULL AND film_total_revenue >= 0
views.description: Select films that have a non-null, non-negative total revenue value. One row per film with its canonical film identifier and total revenue.

views.name: film_actor_assignments_distinct
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fa.actor_id AS actor_id,
  (a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name) AS actor_name,
  fa.film_id AS film_id
FROM film_actor fa
JOIN actor a ON a.actor_id = fa.actor_id
GROUP BY fa.actor_id, fa.film_id, actor_name
views.description: List distinct actor-to-film credit assignments (deduplicated), one row per actor-film pairing. Exclude films with zero credited actors at this stage by ensuring at least one actor per film remains when joined later.

views.name: film_actor_counts_and_shares
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  frv.film_id AS film_id,
  frv.film_total_revenue AS film_total_revenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fa.actor_id) AS film_actor_count,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT fa.actor_id) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE frv.film_total_revenue / COUNT(DISTINCT fa.actor_id)
  END AS actor_share_in_film
FROM film_revenues_valid frv
LEFT JOIN film_actor_assignments_distinct fa
  ON frv.film_id = fa.film_id
GROUP BY frv.film_id, frv.film_total_revenue
views.description: For each film (restricted to valid revenues), count the number of distinct actors credited and compute the per-actor equal share of the film's total revenue (film_total_revenue / film_actor_count). One row per film.

views.name: actor_top3_films_with_ranks_and_avg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fa.actor_id AS actor_id,
  fa.actor_name AS actor_name,
  fac.film_id AS film_id,
  fr.film_title AS film_title,
  fr.film_total_revenue AS film_total_revenue,
  fac.film_actor_count AS film_actor_count,
  fac.actor_share_in_film AS actor_share_in_film,
  -- compute rank of this film within the actor by film_total_revenue desc
  (
    SELECT 1 + COUNT(1)
    FROM film_actor_assignments_distinct fa2
    JOIN film_actor_counts_and_shares fac2 ON fa2.film_id = fac2.film_id
    JOIN film_revenues_valid fr2 ON fac2.film_id = fr2.film_id
    WHERE fa2.actor_id = fa.actor_id
      AND fac2.film_actor_count > 0
      AND fr2.film_total_revenue IS NOT NULL
      AND fac2.film_total_revenue = fac2.film_total_revenue
      AND fr2.film_total_revenue > fr.film_total_revenue
  ) AS rank_within_actor,
  -- actor average share across the actor's top up to 3 films by film_total_revenue
  (
    SELECT AVG(sub.actor_share_in_film)
    FROM (
      SELECT fac3.actor_share_in_film
      FROM film_actor_assignments_distinct fa3
      JOIN film_actor_counts_and_shares fac3 ON fa3.film_id = fac3.film_id
      JOIN film_revenues_valid fr3 ON fac3.film_id = fr3.film_id
      WHERE fa3.actor_id = fa.actor_id
        AND fac3.film_actor_count > 0
        AND fr3.film_total_revenue IS NOT NULL
      ORDER BY fr3.film_total_revenue DESC
      LIMIT 3
    ) AS sub
  ) AS actor_average_share_top3
FROM film_actor_assignments_distinct fa
JOIN film_actor_counts_and_shares fac ON fa.film_id = fac.film_id
JOIN film_revenues_valid fr ON fac.film_id = fr.film_id
WHERE fac.film_actor_count > 0
  AND fr.film_total_revenue IS NOT NULL
views.description: For each actor, join their credited films (only those with valid revenues and with a positive actor count), rank that actor's films by film_total_revenue descending, keep up to the top three films per actor, and compute the actor-level average of actor_share_in_film over those top films. One row per actor-film (top up to 3) including rank and the actor's average share across the kept films.

views.name: top_actors_list
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.actor_id AS actor_id,
  (a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name) AS actor_name,
  COUNT(fa.film_id) AS actor_rank_metric
FROM actor AS a
LEFT JOIN film_actor AS fa
  ON fa.actor_id = a.actor_id
GROUP BY a.actor_id, actor_name
views.description: Identify the set of top actors (the top-ranked actors according to whatever 'top' metric exists in the schema). Produce one row per top actor but do NOT apply the final top-k/limit here so this relation can be reused.

views.name: customer_rentals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.customer_id AS customer_id,
  r.rental_id AS rental_id,
  f.film_id AS film_id,
  fa.actor_id AS actor_id
FROM rental r
JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
JOIN film_actor fa ON f.film_id = fa.film_id
views.description: All customer rental events joined through rental -> inventory -> film -> film_actor (or equivalent) to associate each rental with the customer and each actor who appears in the rented film. One row per rental-event × actor in that film.

views.name: actor_customer_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.actor_id AS actor_id,
  c.customer_id AS customer_id,
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM film_actor fa
    JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = fa.film_id
    JOIN rental r ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
    WHERE fa.actor_id = a.actor_id
      AND r.customer_id = c.customer_id
  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_rented_actor_film
FROM actor a
CROSS JOIN customer c
views.description: For each actor and customer, compute whether the customer has rented at least one film featuring that actor (deduplicate multiple rentals). One row per actor × customer with a boolean or flag indicating membership.

views.name: actor_customer_percentages
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fa.actor_id AS actor_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cr.customer_id) AS customers_who_rented_count,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM customer) AS total_customers_count,
  CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM customer) = 0
    THEN 0.0
    ELSE CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT cr.customer_id) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM customer)
  END AS percentage_of_customers
FROM film_actor fa
JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = fa.film_id
JOIN rental r ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
JOIN customer cr ON cr.customer_id = r.customer_id
GROUP BY fa.actor_id
views.description: For each actor, count distinct customers who have rented a film featuring that actor and compute the percentage relative to the total distinct customer count. This relation should not apply final ordering/limit to top 5; it assumes the caller will restrict to the top actors from top_actors_list.

views.name: customer_payments_and_rentals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.customer_id AS customer_id,
  p.payment_id AS payment_id,
  p.payment_date AS payment_date,
  p.amount AS payment_amount,
  p.rental_id AS rental_id,
  r.inventory_id IS NULL AS __dummy_keep_inventory_not_null, -- preserve ability to join inventory if needed
  inv.film_id AS movie_id,
  f.rating AS movie_rating
FROM payment p
LEFT JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id
LEFT JOIN inventory inv ON r.inventory_id = inv.inventory_id
LEFT JOIN film f ON inv.film_id = f.film_id
views.description: All payment and rental events for customers, one row per payment linked to its rental and movie; include payment amount, payment date, rental id, customer id, and movie id (and movie rating if directly available). This is the base event-level set to compute first rental, total payments, and counts.

views.name: customer_totals_and_rental_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id AS customer_id,
  COALESCE(SUM(p.amount), 0.0) AS total_amount_spent,
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.rental_id) AS total_rentals
FROM customer c
LEFT JOIN payment p ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN rental r ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id
views.description: Per customer aggregates: total amount spent (sum of payment_amount) and total number of rentals (count of distinct rental_id). Keep one row per customer for downstream averages.

views.name: customer_first_rental
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.customer_id AS customer_id,
  p.first_payment_date AS first_payment_date,
  p.first_rental_id AS first_rental_id,
  i.film_id AS first_movie_id,
  f.rating AS first_movie_rating
FROM (
  SELECT
    payment.customer_id,
    -- earliest payment_date per customer
    MIN(payment.payment_date) AS first_payment_date,
    -- deterministic tie-breaker: smallest rental_id among payments that share the earliest date
    (SELECT MIN(p2.rental_id)
     FROM payment p2
     WHERE p2.customer_id = payment.customer_id
       AND p2.payment_date = MIN(payment.payment_date)) AS first_rental_id
  FROM payment
  GROUP BY payment.customer_id
) p
JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.first_rental_id
JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
views.description: Deterministic first rental per customer determined by earliest payment_date; if multiple payments share the earliest date, break ties deterministically by the smallest rental_id (or consistent key). Output the movie (and its rating) for that first rental. One row per customer who has at least one payment.

views.name: rating_level_customer_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cfr.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cfr.first_movie_rating AS first_movie_rating,
  COALESCE(ct.total_amount_spent, 0.0) AS total_amount_spent,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(ct.total_rentals, 0) - 1 > 0 THEN COALESCE(ct.total_rentals, 0) - 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS subsequent_rentals
FROM
  customer_first_rental cfr
LEFT JOIN
  customer_totals_and_rental_counts ct
ON
  cfr.customer_id = ct.customer_id
views.description: For each rating (the rating of each customer's first movie), combine the per-customer aggregates with the first-rental rating and compute per-customer subsequent_rentals = greatest(total_rentals - 1, 0). Produce one row per customer-with-rating to allow final averaging by rating.

views.name: top_customers_set
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id
FROM customer c
JOIN customer_totals_and_rental_counts t
  ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE t.total_amount_spent IS NOT NULL
  AND t.total_amount_spent > 0
views.description: The set of customers that are marked as 'our top 10 paying customers' in the source data; one row per customer that belongs to that provided top-10 cohort.

views.name: customer_month_payments
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.customer_id AS customer_id,
  STRFTIME('%Y-%m', p.payment_date) AS month,
  SUM(p.amount) AS payment_amount
FROM payment AS p
GROUP BY p.customer_id, STRFTIME('%Y-%m', p.payment_date)
views.description: For all customers (not yet filtered), compute total payment amount per customer per source month as recorded in the payments data (one row per customer-month). Do not apply top-10 filter here so relation is reusable.

views.name: top_customers_month_payments
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cms.customer_id,
  cms.month,
  cms.payment_amount
FROM
  customer_month_payments AS cms
JOIN
  top_customers_set AS tcs
ON
  cms.customer_id = tcs.customer_id
views.description: Restrict the per-customer-month payments to only those customers present in the top_customers_set by joining the two relations; one row per top-customer-month.

views.name: month_to_next_diff
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cm.customer_id,
  cm.year_month AS month_earlier,
  lead(cm.year_month) OVER (PARTITION BY cm.customer_id ORDER BY cm.year_month) AS month_later,
  abs(cm.month_total_amount - lead(cm.month_total_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY cm.customer_id ORDER BY cm.year_month)) AS abs_payment_diff
FROM customer_monthly_totals cm
views.description: For each top customer, order their months chronologically and use a lead/lag window to pair each month with the immediately following month, computing the absolute difference in payment_amount between the month and the next month. Produce one row per customer-month (where a next month exists) with the earlier-month, later-month, and absolute difference.

views.name: staff_created_rentals
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rental.rental_id AS rental_id,
  store.store_id AS store_id,
  rental.rental_date AS created_at
FROM rental
JOIN inventory ON rental.inventory_id = inventory.inventory_id
JOIN store ON inventory.store_id = store.store_id
WHERE rental.staff_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: Select rental orders that were created by store staff (exclude rentals not created by staff), projecting rental id, store id, and the rental creation timestamp.

views.name: rental_year_month
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rental.rental_id AS rental_id,
  COALESCE(inv.store_id, staff_created_rentals.store_id, store.store_id) AS store_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', rental.rental_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', rental.rental_date) AS INTEGER) AS month
FROM rental
LEFT JOIN inventory AS inv
  ON rental.inventory_id = inv.inventory_id
LEFT JOIN store
  ON inv.store_id = store.store_id
LEFT JOIN staff_created_rentals
  ON rental.rental_id = staff_created_rentals.rental_id
views.description: Normalize each staff-created rental to extract the calendar year and month number from the creation timestamp (one row per rental preserved).

views.name: store_monthly_rental_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.store_id AS store_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', r.rental_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', r.rental_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  COUNT(r.rental_id) AS total_rentals
FROM rental r
JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
GROUP BY
  i.store_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', r.rental_date) AS INTEGER),
  CAST(strftime('%m', r.rental_date) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Aggregate to count the number of staff-created rentals per store per calendar year and month.

views.name: store_top_months
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  smr.store_id,
  smr.year,
  smr.month,
  smr.total_rentals,
  CASE WHEN smr.total_rentals = max_per_store.max_total THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS rank_or_flag
FROM
  store_monthly_rental_counts AS smr
JOIN (
  SELECT
    store_id,
    MAX(total_rentals) AS max_total
  FROM
    store_monthly_rental_counts
  GROUP BY
    store_id
) AS max_per_store
  ON smr.store_id = max_per_store.store_id
views.description: For each store, rank or mark year-month groups by total_rentals to identify the maximum(s) per store; keep all ties for the top count.
